correctness.rationale: The strict 0-or-2 best-response equation is encoded exactly by the adjacency/popcount test. The exhaustive program covers all 1+2+8+64+1024+32768 labeled graph masks and all their binary profiles, finding 0 failures below six and 300 at six. The entire failure set equals the disjoint relabeling orbits (180 and 120) of the two explicit graphs. Their nonexistence also has a separate complete structural proof using degree-two parity and four cases for the 3-sun. A separate edge-by-edge implementation was compared for 10,816 finite graph-state checks. No asymptotic conclusion rests on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The first failure size and complete minimal obstruction types are natural finite structural invariants for a strict homogeneous rule with NP-complete existence. The second eight-edge witness is a distinct smaller-edge test case than the published 3-sun, and the exact two-class first layer informs minimal gadget selection and finite model validation. The sharp complete classification goes beyond rerunning a known table or a routine sanity check, though it remains explicitly finite.
